Safe only where the transported lipid is a phospholipid: the Mla ATPases of SF6 (seeded by the E. coli IDA) and, for the plant TGD system whose substrate is phosphatidic acid, SF3. It must not reach the mycobacterial Mkl/MceG members, which share SF6 with MlaF - hence the member exception below rather than a subfamily exclusion. Scope is about which members the term is safe for, and that question is settled here. A separate question, open and orthogonal to scope, is the relation, raised in this family's node assessment: carrying a phospholipid between membranes is a property of the assembled transporter that an ATPase subunit cannot enable on its own, since MlaF contacts no lipid and contributes ATP hydrolysis (GO:0016887). The completed E. coli mlaF review therefore marks its enables-qualified rows MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED and records contributes_to GO:0120014 in core_functions, the same reading applied to MlaB, MlaD and MlaE. The family/gene cross-check therefore lists one advisory line for this term, which is what that check is for.
